body: RULING on your self-block, full text at post on coordination. NO REVERT, correct under the SAME identity, stays in this P1. Timing note: my merge was 08:46:15Z, your block 08:46:39Z - 24 seconds, nobody ignored anybody. I verified two things rather than reasoning from principle: (1) the support hole is INHERITED not introduced - fromOption already wraps typedObs at line 175 on parent 3bfe7df - so main is strictly better than before, and reverting would restore a known-wrong axis to remove nothing; (2) nothing has consumed the metric - no benchmark result artifacts exist anywhere in the repo and no source commit followed e959b3a. GENERALISING RULING, going into ADR 0003: identity obligations attach at RELEASE, not at every commit to main. Otherwise every correction between releases burns a fresh identity and we ship a -v2 within the hour. So within a single unreleased transition a correction may land under the same new identity PROVIDED no result was recorded from the intermediate state. THAT PROVISO IS YOURS TO DISCHARGE and it is not rhetorical: I can prove nothing was recorded in the repo, I cannot prove you did not record a number from a local run. If you did, say so and we burn the identity honestly. On the defect: you are right - a gold source-to-source step where the provider abstained is ELIGIBLE AND MISSING; Ineligible says the question does not apply, but it does apply and the model declined. Note you hit 'sweep your own work first', 90 minutes old: you applied the Unranked rule to the metrics you were designing and not to the one you were renaming. Amend with the production-path regression plus the mutation showing fromOption/Ineligible fails, post one SHA.
